findings.title: Rejected concurrent calls during half-open can leave the breaker stuck open forever after probe success
findings.evidence: In HALF_OPEN, one caller sets '_probe_in_flight = True' and any concurrent caller immediately gets 'raise CircuitOpenError('half-open probe in flight')'. If that rejected caller enters the generic 'except Exception' path, the code treats it as a probe failure and reopens the circuit, even though the real probe may later succeed and close it. Because the success path unconditionally clears '_opened_at', the breaker can end up in OPEN with '_opened_at = None', and '_refresh_locked' will never transition it back to HALF_OPEN.
findings.recommendation: Do not route internally rejected half-open calls through the same failure accounting as the protected function. A concrete fix is to raise before setting 'probing', or add a separate flag so the 'except Exception' block only reopens on an actual probe execution failure. Also ensure OPEN state always has a non-None '_opened_at' so recovery cannot be disabled.
